title: Initial 220 timeout is not shorter than five minutes
natural_language: TCP 连接建立后等待初始 220 greeting 时，SMTP 客户端不应在 300000 ms 前因该阶段超时而放弃。
time_source: RFC 5321 recommended minimum; Exim command_timeout default is 5*60 seconds
benchmark_reachability_note: ProFuzzBench starts Exim with -bd as an inbound TCP/25 server; this outbound smtp_setup_conn path requires a separate queue-runner/client harness and a withholding peer server.
property_scope: Classic outbound SMTP initial greeting after a successful TCP connection; implicit SMTPS is excluded from this source profile.

ap_definitions.smtp_waiting_initial_220: smtp_connect returns a valid socket in smtp_setup_conn, opening one correlated initial-220 obligation before the later smtp_read_response call
ap_definitions.smtp_initial_220_timeout: the initial-greeting smtp_read_response returns false with errno==ETIMEDOUT for that same connection before a valid initial 220 response

correlation_key: outbound SMTP connection identity + remote host/address + delivery attempt
projection_rule: one successful-connect/initial-greeting obligation per timed word; a greeting, peer close, non-timeout I/O error, or delivery-attempt teardown closes only that generation; identifiers remain fields
monitor_instantiation: EXACTLY_ONE_TRIGGER_PER_PROJECTED_WORD; correlate the successful connect to its initial smtp_read_response outcome before projection

event_contract.trigger: emit once immediately after smtp_connect returns a nonnegative socket at smtp.c:1544-1549
event_contract.timeout: emit only when the correlated initial smtp_read_response at smtp.c:1638-1643 returns false with errno==ETIMEDOUT, before RESPONSE_FAILED
event_contract.non_timeout_outcomes: valid 220, EOF, protocol error, peer close, and other errno values close/cancel the generation without emitting smtp_initial_220_timeout
event_contract.clock_basis: absolute integer milliseconds from the successful-connect event; no RFC constant scaling

instrumentation_timing: emit start once after successful smtp_connect; after the initial smtp_read_response returns false, inspect errno and emit timeout only for ETIMEDOUT before the RESPONSE_FAILED jump; use smtp_transport_option_defaults:222 as profile evidence
audit_disposition_note: The original card started the event at smtp_read_response rather than successful TCP connect, omitted common ETIMEDOUT source anchors, and did not disclose that the ProFuzzBench server harness cannot reach this client path.
independent_audit_note: Original disposition FIX retained above; role, reachability, connect-time trigger, timeout source chain, and one-generation event contract are now explicit. Lower-bound semantics still does not require timeout at five minutes.
review_question: 确认是否新增 outbound-client/queue-runner harness；若只运行 ProFuzzBench server campaign，本卡应留在 client-role 附录。
limitations: RFC 5321 uses SHOULD for the recommended minimum. This fixed Exim client path is absent from the inbound ProFuzzBench campaign, and a real 300-second wait has LOW wall-clock fuzzing triggerability without a validated virtual clock.
pointwise_semantics: pointwise event positions with absolute integer milliseconds; mathematical_mitl uses standard MITL, while mightyppl_formula uses MightyPPL's weak finite-word G* operator
finite_end_semantics: one correlated obligation generation per finite word; append a terminal position strictly beyond every bounded deadline so the supplied oracle is decisive; no overlapping trigger generations

title: MAIL response timeout is not shorter than five minutes
natural_language: 客户端发出 MAIL FROM 后等待响应时，不应在 300000 ms 前因 MAIL 阶段超时而放弃。
time_source: RFC 5321 recommended minimum; Exim command_timeout default is 300 seconds
benchmark_reachability_note: Requires Exim outbound delivery plus a controlled peer SMTP server; the benchmark's inbound daemon path does not execute smtp_write_mail_and_rcpt_cmds.
property_scope: Outbound SMTP MAIL response, covering both direct and PIPELINING paths after the MAIL command is actually flushed.

ap_definitions.smtp_mail_response_wait_started: flush_buffer successfully transmits a buffer containing the correlated MAIL FROM command; the adapter assigns that command a transaction-generation ordinal before response projection
ap_definitions.smtp_mail_response_timeout: the response read associated with that pending MAIL generation returns false with errno==ETIMEDOUT

correlation_key: outbound connection + SMTP transaction generation + MAIL command sequence
projection_rule: decode each successfully flushed command buffer, correlate the pending MAIL response slot, then project exactly one MAIL generation per timed word; command ordinals remain fields
monitor_instantiation: EXACTLY_ONE_TRIGGER_PER_PROJECTED_WORD; one flushed MAIL command and its response outcome constitute one monitor instance

event_contract.trigger: emit once after flush_buffer successfully sends the buffer containing this MAIL command, not when the command is merely queued and not when its response read later begins
event_contract.timeout: emit only for the pending-MAIL smtp_read_response outcome with errno==ETIMEDOUT in either sync_responses or the direct path
event_contract.non_timeout_outcomes: 2xx, 4xx/5xx, malformed response, EOF, peer close, and other I/O errors close the generation without smtp_mail_response_timeout
event_contract.clock_basis: absolute integer milliseconds from successful wire flush; no timeout scaling

auxiliary_source_mappings.role: MAIL command and direct response path

instrumentation_timing: at successful flush_buffer return, parse the just-sent command buffer and emit one start for its MAIL ordinal; emit timeout only when that pending MAIL response read returns false with errno==ETIMEDOUT
audit_disposition_note: The original event conflated successful MAIL flush with the later sync_responses read, used a composite non-symbol, omitted the common timeout chain, and did not disclose server-benchmark unreachability.
independent_audit_note: Original disposition FIX retained above; successful flush is now the trigger, direct and pipelined response paths are separate auxiliary mappings, and role/reachability are explicit.
review_question: 确认 outbound adapter 能从一次 flush 中恢复 MAIL/RCPT/DATA ordinal；若无 client harness，本卡不进入 server 主实验。
limitations: SHOULD-level minimum. Response arrival, connection close, and other I/O errors are not timeout APs. The current ProFuzzBench Exim server campaign cannot reach this path, and a 300-second real wait has LOW fuzzing triggerability.
pointwise_semantics: pointwise event positions with absolute integer milliseconds; mathematical_mitl uses standard MITL, while mightyppl_formula uses MightyPPL's weak finite-word G* operator
finite_end_semantics: one correlated obligation generation per finite word; append a terminal position strictly beyond every bounded deadline so the supplied oracle is decisive; no overlapping trigger generations

title: RCPT response timeout is not shorter than five minutes
natural_language: 客户端发出每个 RCPT TO 后等待相应响应时，不应在 300000 ms 前因该 RCPT 阶段超时而放弃。
time_source: RFC 5321 recommended minimum; Exim command_timeout default is 300 seconds
benchmark_reachability_note: Requires Exim outbound delivery and a controlled peer server; the inbound daemon benchmark does not execute this RCPT client path.
property_scope: One outbound SMTP RCPT response generation after that RCPT command is actually flushed, including PIPELINING correlation by recipient ordinal.

ap_definitions.smtp_rcpt_response_wait_started: flush_buffer successfully transmits a buffer containing the correlated RCPT command and assigns it a transaction-local RCPT ordinal
ap_definitions.smtp_rcpt_response_timeout: sync_responses maps the pending response slot to that RCPT ordinal and its smtp_read_response returns false with errno==ETIMEDOUT

correlation_key: outbound connection + SMTP transaction generation + RCPT ordinal/address field
projection_rule: decode each successful flush, assign RCPT ordinals, correlate sync_responses slots in order, then spawn one obligation projection per RCPT ordinal; address remains an event field
monitor_instantiation: EXACTLY_ONE_TRIGGER_PER_PROJECTED_WORD; each flushed RCPT ordinal and its single response outcome are monitored separately

event_contract.trigger: emit once after the command buffer containing this RCPT is successfully flushed, not at the later response-read call
event_contract.timeout: emit only from sync_responses when the slot correlated to this RCPT ordinal takes the errno==ETIMEDOUT branch
event_contract.non_timeout_outcomes: accepted/rejected response, malformed response, peer close, EOF, and other I/O errors close the generation without the timeout AP
event_contract.clock_basis: absolute integer milliseconds from successful wire flush

auxiliary_source_mappings.role: RCPT command enqueue/flush and sync invocation

instrumentation_timing: emit start after the successful command-buffer flush for this RCPT ordinal; in sync_responses emit timeout only after ordinal correlation and only on the complete errno==ETIMEDOUT branch at lines 816-825
audit_disposition_note: The original RCPT response mapping was sound, but the trigger was the later read rather than actual flush, the timeout branch range ended early, and role/benchmark reachability were missing.
independent_audit_note: Original disposition FIX retained above; full ETIMEDOUT branch, successful-flush trigger, separate source mappings, and one-monitor-per-RCPT contract are now explicit.
review_question: 确认 adapter 从 flush 顺序和 PENDING_DEFER 扫描得到相同 RCPT ordinal；若只 fuzz inbound server，本卡留在 client 附录。
limitations: The RFC notes that list/alias processing can need longer; this card asserts only the recommended minimum. The path is unreachable in the current server harness and a real 300-second delay is LOW-triggerability.

finite_end_semantics: one correlated obligation generation per finite word; append a terminal position strictly beyond every bounded deadline so the supplied oracle is decisive; no overlapping trigger generations

title: DATA initiation timeout is not shorter than two minutes
natural_language: 客户端发出 DATA 后等待 354 Start Input 时，不应在 120000 ms 前因 DATA-initiation 阶段超时。
time_source: RFC 5321 recommended minimum; Exim uses the longer 300-second command_timeout default
benchmark_reachability_note: Requires Exim outbound classic-DATA delivery and a peer that withholds 354; the benchmark only drives Exim's inbound server.
property_scope: Outbound classic SMTP DATA command awaiting its 354 response; CHUNKING/BDAT is excluded because that path does not send DATA.

ap_definitions.smtp_data_354_wait_started: smtp_write_command(..., FALSE, DATA) successfully flushes the correlated classic-DATA command and opens one 354-wait generation
ap_definitions.smtp_data_354_timeout: the pending-DATA response slot correlated by sync_responses returns false with errno==ETIMEDOUT before a 354 reply

correlation_key: outbound connection + SMTP transaction generation + DATA command ordinal
projection_rule: after successful DATA flush, correlate the pending_DATA slot after any preceding pipelined MAIL/RCPT slots, then project one DATA-initiation generation per transaction
monitor_instantiation: EXACTLY_ONE_TRIGGER_PER_PROJECTED_WORD; one successfully flushed DATA command and its pending_DATA response outcome form one monitor instance

event_contract.trigger: emit once after smtp_write_command(..., FALSE, DATA) returns a successful flush at smtp.c:2659-2665
event_contract.timeout: emit only when the subsequently correlated pending_DATA smtp_read_response expecting 3xx returns false with errno==ETIMEDOUT
event_contract.non_timeout_outcomes: 354, other SMTP reply, malformed response, EOF, peer close, or other I/O error closes the generation without smtp_data_354_timeout
event_contract.clock_basis: absolute integer milliseconds from successful DATA wire flush

instrumentation_timing: emit start after the DATA command's successful forced flush; when sync_responses reaches that pending_DATA slot, emit timeout only for false return with errno==ETIMEDOUT
audit_disposition_note: The original card conflated successful DATA flush with the later pending_DATA response read, used a composite symbol, omitted the timeout chain, and lacked client/server reachability scope.
independent_audit_note: Original disposition FIX retained above; the wire-flush trigger, pending_DATA response correlation, classic-DATA scope, common timeout sources, and role are now explicit.
review_question: 确认 adapter 把 354 wait 与 message-body block 和 final-250 generations 分离；server-only campaign 不收录本卡为可达主性质。
limitations: This lower bound does not claim timeout at two minutes. Exim's default is longer, the current inbound server harness cannot reach the path, and a real 120-second stall remains LOW-triggerability.
pointwise_semantics: pointwise event positions with absolute integer milliseconds; mathematical_mitl uses standard MITL, while mightyppl_formula uses MightyPPL's weak finite-word G* operator
finite_end_semantics: one correlated obligation generation per finite word; append a terminal position strictly beyond every bounded deadline so the supplied oracle is decisive; no overlapping trigger generations

title: Each DATA block send timeout is not shorter than three minutes
natural_language: 传输一个 DATA 数据块并等待该 TCP SEND 完成时，不应在 180000 ms 前因 data-block send timeout 放弃。
time_parameter: minimum timeout per TCP SEND data block
time_source: RFC 5321 recommended minimum; Exim data_timeout default is 300 seconds
benchmark_reachability_note: The main hook is shared code, but this property requires the outbound smtp_deliver data context; inbound TCP/25 server fuzzing does not create it.
property_scope: One timed transport_write_block invocation carrying classic outbound SMTP DATA; non-SMTP transports and extension-specific BDAT claims are excluded.

ap_definitions.smtp_data_block_send_wait_started: one SMTP-guarded transport_write_block invocation starts with transport_write_timeout copied from smtp_deliver's data_timeout; the event does not assert that the first write is already known to block
ap_definitions.smtp_data_block_send_timeout: that same invocation returns false with errno==ETIMEDOUT through sigalrm_seen or exhausted local_timeout

correlation_key: outbound connection + SMTP transaction generation + monotonically increasing DATA block ordinal
projection_rule: guard the generic function by outbound SMTP data context, allocate one block ordinal on function entry, emit exactly one trigger for that invocation, then project it independently; loop retries do not open new generations
monitor_instantiation: EXACTLY_ONE_TRIGGER_PER_PROJECTED_WORD; one SMTP DATA transport_write_block invocation, including all of its partial-write retries, is one monitor instance

event_contract.trigger: emit once per guarded transport_write_block invocation before its first timed write/alarm; never emit again for loop retries
event_contract.timeout: emit only on the sigalrm_seen ETIMEDOUT return at transport.c:257-260 or exhausted-local_timeout return at 302-306
event_contract.guard: outbound SMTP delivery context + target SMTP socket fd + smtp_command equivalent to sending data block + transport_write_timeout sourced from smtp data_timeout
event_contract.non_timeout_outcomes: successful full/partial completion, EPIPE, EAGAIN recovery, ERRNO_WRITEINCOMPLETE, and non-timeout errno values close without smtp_data_block_send_timeout
event_contract.clock_basis: one absolute remaining-time budget per transport_write_block invocation

auxiliary_source_mappings.role: SMTP data-timeout selection and outbound message write
buffer flushes that invoke the primary hook

instrumentation_timing: after verifying the SMTP outbound data guard, emit one start per transport_write_block invocation before its first timed write; do not re-emit inside the retry loop; emit timeout only at the two ETIMEDOUT returns; smtp_deliver:2736-2738 proves the selected data_timeout profile
audit_disposition_note: The transport.c primary hook was correct, but the original contract could emit a trigger for every alarm retry, described a write as already blocked before calling it, and did not guard the generic transport function or disclose role reachability.
independent_audit_note: Original disposition FIX retained above. The primary hook remains transport_write_block:216-306; SMTP guard, exactly-once invocation trigger, two timeout exits, role, and reachability are now explicit.
review_question: 确认 instrumentation 能取得显式 SMTP context/fd/block ordinal，而不是依赖易冲突的全局字符串；若不能，保留为未实现 hook。
limitations: RFC 5321 applies a separate minimum timer to each classic DATA buffer; total message duration is unbounded. The generic source hook must exclude every non-SMTP caller, and the real 180-second threshold is LOW-triggerability without validated virtual time.

finite_end_semantics: one correlated obligation generation per finite word; append a terminal position strictly beyond every bounded deadline so the supplied oracle is decisive; no overlapping trigger generations

protocol_extension: RFC 5321 classic DATA client timeout recommendation
title: Classic DATA termination timeout is not shorter than ten minutes
natural_language: 客户端通过 classic DATA 发送 final period 后等待 250 OK 时，不应在 600000 ms 前因 final-response timeout 放弃。
time_source: RFC 5321 recommended minimum; Exim final_timeout default is 10*60 seconds
benchmark_reachability_note: Requires an outbound classic-DATA delivery and peer server that withholds the final reply; the benchmark's inbound daemon path does not execute it.
property_scope: Classic RFC 5321 DATA final period and the single non-LMTP final response; CHUNKING/BDAT, PRDR, LMTP, and implicit extensions are excluded.

ap_definitions.smtp_final_250_wait_started: non-CHUNKING smtp_deliver successfully transmits the final data buffer containing the terminating period and enters the non-LMTP final-response phase
ap_definitions.smtp_final_250_timeout: the corresponding non-PRDR, non-LMTP smtp_read_response expecting 2xx returns false with errno==ETIMEDOUT before a 250 response

correlation_key: outbound connection + SMTP transaction generation + end-of-data marker
projection_rule: require classic DATA/non-LMTP/non-PRDR context, correlate the successfully sent terminating-period buffer to the following final response, and project one generation per transaction
monitor_instantiation: EXACTLY_ONE_TRIGGER_PER_PROJECTED_WORD; one classic DATA end marker and its single final-response outcome form one monitor instance

event_contract.trigger: emit once after transport_write_message succeeds for non-CHUNKING DATA and smtp_command changes to end of data at smtp.c:2766-2772
event_contract.timeout: emit only when the correlated non-LMTP final smtp_read_response at 2815-2827 returns false with errno==ETIMEDOUT
event_contract.non_timeout_outcomes: 250, 4xx/5xx, malformed response, EOF, peer close, and other I/O errors close the generation without smtp_final_250_timeout
event_contract.excluded_paths: CHUNKING/BDAT, PRDR preliminary/partial responses, and LMTP per-recipient responses
event_contract.clock_basis: absolute integer milliseconds from successful classic end-of-data transmission

instrumentation_timing: guard classic DATA/non-CHUNKING/non-LMTP/non-PRDR context; emit start once after the terminating-period write succeeds and before the final read; emit timeout only for that read's ETIMEDOUT outcome
audit_disposition_note: The original card extended RFC 5321's classic final-period evidence to last BDAT/PRDR/LMTP, omitted the common timeout chain, and lacked client-role reachability disclosure.
independent_audit_note: Original disposition FIX retained above; the property is now restricted to classic DATA and its single non-LMTP final response, with role and timeout source chain explicit.
review_question: 确认实验是否只启用 classic DATA；若要覆盖 BDAT/PRDR/LMTP，必须分别提取扩展规范性质，不能复用本卡主张。
limitations: A 4xx/5xx response, peer close, or other I/O error is not a timeout. Extension paths are excluded. The client path is absent from the current server harness, and a real 600-second wait is LOW-triggerability.
pointwise_semantics: pointwise event positions with absolute integer milliseconds; mathematical_mitl uses standard MITL, while mightyppl_formula uses MightyPPL's weak finite-word G* operator
finite_end_semantics: one correlated obligation generation per finite word; append a terminal position strictly beyond every bounded deadline so the supplied oracle is decisive; no overlapping trigger generations

protocol_extension: RFC 5321 server timeout recommendation; Exim plaintext profile
title: Plaintext server command-read timeout is not shorter than five minutes
natural_language: plaintext SMTP server 的输入 buffer 为空并等待发送方下一段命令输入时，不应在 300000 ms 前因 command-phase receive timeout 关闭连接。
standard_excerpt: An SMTP server SHOULD have a timeout of at least 5 minutes
time_parameter: minimum server wait for next command
time_source: RFC 5321 recommended minimum; Exim smtp_receive_timeout default is 5*60 seconds
benchmark_reachability_note: ProFuzzBench drives this plaintext inbound daemon role, but a normal AFLNet testcase is far shorter than the real 300-second deadline; a long trace or validated virtual clock is required for timeout feedback.
property_scope: Exim plaintext SMTP command phase only; DATA-phase receive timeout, STARTTLS tls_getc paths, batched input, and implicit TLS are excluded.

ap_definitions.smtp_server_command_wait_started: while smtp_read_command has command_timeout_handler installed, plaintext smtp_getc finds its input buffer empty and arms smtp_receive_timeout immediately before read
ap_definitions.smtp_server_command_idle_timeout: that same command-read generation reaches command_timeout_handler because the armed receive alarm expires and closes the correlated connection

projection_rule: spawn one plaintext command-read generation each time smtp_getc arms a receive alarm under smtp_read_command; bytes/read completion, command completion, phase change, or connection close ends that generation before the next one
monitor_instantiation: EXACTLY_ONE_TRIGGER_PER_PROJECTED_WORD; each plaintext smtp_getc alarm arm in command phase is a separate monitor instance

event_contract.trigger: emit once at smtp_in.c:424 when smtp_read_command's command_timeout_handler is active and plaintext smtp_getc arms smtp_receive_timeout for an empty buffer
event_contract.timeout: emit only on entry to command_timeout_handler for the same connection/generation
event_contract.non_timeout_outcomes: read data, complete command, EOF, non-timeout read error, DATA-phase transition, STARTTLS transition, or connection teardown closes/cancels without the timeout AP
event_contract.excluded_paths: tls-openssl tls_getc, tls-gnu tls_getc, DATA receive handler, and batched input
event_contract.clock_basis: absolute integer milliseconds from the individual plaintext command-read alarm arm

auxiliary_source_mappings.role: command-phase signal-handler installation and read loop
command timeout outcome and connection close

instrumentation_timing: emit start only when plaintext smtp_getc arms the receive alarm while smtp_read_command has installed command_timeout_handler; emit timeout only inside that handler and correlate by accepted connection/read generation
audit_disposition_note: The original card made a generic server/STARTTLS claim while only mapping plaintext smtp_getc, omitted smtp_read_command's handler context, and rated a real five-minute wait HIGH-triggerability.
independent_audit_note: Original disposition FIX retained above; the card is now explicitly plaintext command-phase, maps handler installation and timeout outcome, and distinguishes role reachability from practical deadline triggerability.

limitations: This card covers each plaintext command-read alarm generation, not an absolute whole-line deadline and not DATA/TLS reads. Although the server role is benchmark-reachable, the real 300-second deadline has LOW per-testcase triggerability without validated virtual time.
